matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When attempting to fix the equation, first try moving a single matchstick within the same character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation is invalid, start by exploring intra‑character moves before considering inter‑character relocations.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick within a character and leaving a single angled stick behind, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, verify that each resulting character matches a recognized Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick move, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Failing to check that a transformed character is still a valid numeral, leading to an invalid symbol like a lone diagonal.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not correspond to any Roman numeral; ensure that removing a diagonal does not leave an isolated angled stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is moved from a character like X or V.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from an X and not using it elsewhere, leaving a single diagonal stick.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equation, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral to another but creating an invalid numeral on the source side.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation after any transformation; the equality must hold.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming that all symbols are valid.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without checking that the numeric values actually match.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If a stick is taken from the '=' sign, ensure the remaining symbol still forms a valid equality sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal line from '=', leaving a single line that is not a valid '='.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After the move, check that each multi‑character numeral follows standard Roman numeral ordering rules.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming individual characters are valid, before arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Creating a numeral like 'IXIV' that violates Roman numeral ordering.

matchstick.title: Intra-character diagonal transformation (V↔X)
matchstick.principle: When a character is V or X (both made of two diagonal sticks), moving one diagonal within the same character can transform V into X or X into V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation involves V or X and intra‑character moves are being considered.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, resulting in an invalid character.

matchstick.title: Transform '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick to an adjacent I
matchstick.principle: When a '+' operator and an 'I' numeral are present, moving the vertical stick from '+' to the 'I' (or to a position that creates an extra 'I') turns '+' into a valid '-' and increases the numeral's value, often fixing the arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains a '+' and at least one 'I' that can be augmented without breaking Roman numeral syntax.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' but not attaching it to a valid numeral, leaving an orphaned stick.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler fixes that can be achieved by reshaping a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First explore intra‑character stick relocations, such as converting X to V or V to X, before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: When a diagonal stick is taken from X or V, the remaining single diagonal does not correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that any diagonal removed from X or V is placed elsewhere to form a valid character, never leaving an isolated diagonal.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may focus on symbol validity and overlook whether the numeric equality actually holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After confirming all symbols are valid, compute the numeric values of both sides and verify the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think changing an operator can fix the equation without checking the overall structure and the necessity of a valid equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never alter the '=' sign unless you can simultaneously create a new valid '=', and always verify that exactly one equality sign remains.

matchstick.description: Creating nonstandard Roman numeral forms (e.g., IXIV) that are not valid according to standard Roman numeral rules
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may combine symbols in ways that produce invalid numeral sequences.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any transformation, check that each multi‑character numeral follows standard Roman numeral ordering and subtraction rules.
